questions.q: What does the 'Future Enterable' period status allow?
options: Full transaction activity, including posting
Journal entry, but not posting
No activity of any kind
Only reconciliation reports
questions.explain: Future Enterable allows journal entry to be recorded ahead of the period opening, but posting is not yet allowed.

questions.q: What is the Close Monitor / period close checklist used for?
options: Formatting payment files
Releasing invoice holds
Calculating depreciation
Showing exactly which specific prerequisites are met or outstanding before a period can close
questions.explain: Rather than a single opaque 'can't close' message, the Close Monitor identifies precisely which prerequisites (like unposted journals or untransferred subledger batches) remain outstanding.

questions.q: What were the two specific blockers preventing October from closing at Thornfield Materials Holdings?
options: 6 unposted GL journals (one referencing a disabled account) and one Payables batch accounted Final but not transferred to GL
A duplicate invoice and a misapplied receipt
A failed Journal Import and a security issue
An unreconciled bank statement
questions.explain: The Close Monitor identified six unposted journals and one untransferred Payables batch as the two unmet prerequisites blocking the close.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is usually true about the root causes behind a period-close failure?
options: They are always a brand-new type of problem unique to period close
They can only be fixed by Oracle support
They are almost always variations of problems already covered elsewhere (like a disabled account or an untransferred batch), just surfaced by the close checklist
They require permanently closing the period
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes that period-close tickets are usually the same kinds of issues covered in earlier lessons (posting, transfer, accounting failures), discovered via the close checklist rather than an individual complaint.

questions.q: Why was it useful to recognize the untransferred Payables batch as matching the pattern from Lesson 8 or Lesson 19?
options: It wasn't useful — period-close issues require a completely different diagnostic approach
It let the consultant apply the already-known diagnostic steps (check for a timing gap vs. an intentional exclusion) instead of starting from scratch
It meant the batch should simply be deleted
It meant the whole ledger needed to be rebuilt
questions.explain: Recognizing the familiar pattern let the consultant quickly determine whether this was a timing gap (Lesson 8) or an intentional Transfer to GL exclusion (Lesson 19), rather than treating it as an unfamiliar problem.
